external_ground_truth.reason: All onboard position channels can share localization or inertial biases.
external_ground_truth.required_artifact: fixed-camera video with visible floor reference marks

findings.conclusion: the canonical bag contains an elevated odometry gap
FAST-LIO logged neither a recovery event nor a permanent odometry lock during the patrol
original-to-runtime CSV conversion is exactly reproducible within CSV precision
FAST-LIO trajectory itself deviated materially from the runtime CSV
the follower had elevated odometry age or prolonged reuse of one odometry update
this patrol cannot be cryptographically linked to a route-recording blackbox
captured source/executable identities stayed unchanged during the run
Unitree state reported a motor-lost count or a nonzero sport error code
FAST-LIO and body IMU relative orientation changed materially during the run
onboard logs cannot prove whether FAST-LIO's reported XY equals the dog's true floor position; use the fixed camera/floor-marker record for that final distinction

follower_control_trace.interpretation: Reusing one odometry sample for two 20 Hz control cycles is normal when FAST-LIO publishes at 10 Hz. Risk is indicated by large odom age or long consecutive reuse, not by dropping intermediate sensor frames by itself.

measured_response.note: SportModeState is an onboard feedback source, not external metric ground truth.

sensor_body_alignment.interpretation: A stable relative rotation supports a rigid mount and consistent onboard attitude sources. Its absolute value is not external floor truth and may include differing yaw origins.

localization_configuration.mounting_note: These values describe the LiDAR-to-LiDAR-IMU/configured transform. They do not independently measure the physical LiDAR-to-dog-body mounting angle.
